definition: Marvin Lee Minsky (August 9, 1927 – January 24, 2016) was an American mathematician who conducted research in the cognitive and computer science aspects of artificial intelligence (AI).
details: Pioneered cognitive science, neural network theory (Perceptrons), symbolic AI, and robotics. After three years as a Junior Fellow of the Harvard Society of Fellows, Minsky joined the faculty at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in 1958 and spent the rest of his career at that institution. There, he co-founded MIT's AI laboratory, among other initiatives, and wrote extensively about AI and philosophy.

explainer.lead: Marvin Minsky was an American cognitive scientist (1927–2016). His work spans artificial intelligence, cognitive science, philosophy of mind and computer science.
explainer.knownFor: Notable works include Perceptrons, Society of Mind, The Emotion Machine and Computation: Finite and Infinite Machines.

contributions.name: He was elected to the U.S. National Academy of Sciences in 1973 and the U.S. National Academy of Engineering in 1989, and was inducted into IEEE Intelligent Systems' AI Hall of Fame for contributions to AI and intelligent systems in 2011.
In 1951, Minsky built SNARC, which is often considered the first artificial neural network.
Minsky also developed several other AI models.
His paper "A Framework for Representing Knowledge" created a new paradigm in knowledge representation.
